newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday in quiet trading awaiting publication of the April consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 to 104.92

"Trading was very quiet although volumes were high," said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment. "There was active demand for unlinked bonds on forecasts that inflation in the coming year will be low, around seven percent," he said.
"CPI-linked bonds had positive trading as well, with stronger demand for long-term bonds," he said.
"Traders are waiting to see what April's CPI will be -- forecasts are that it will be around 1.2 percent," Alt said.
April's CPI will be published on May 15. The CPI is usually high in April due to the Passover holiday.

"There was demand for all types of bonds in trading today but prices and yields remained unchanged. Only long-term CPI-linked bonds registered a minor change in yields," said a trader at a major financial company. "Yields of short-term CPI-linked bonds are at 4.4 percent and those of long-term CPI-linked bonds are at 4.2 percent."
"The yields of the Makams have been stable at 13.9 percent already for a long time," he said.

He added that traders were awaiting the publication of April's CPI. "Traders are not holding their breath," he said. "People expect the CPI to be seasonally high, and don't expect surprises. They also don't expect interest rates to go down. All these expectations are already included in the prices," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
